findings.element: Matching-rules overlay — Close (×) button and click-outside-the-sheet (backdrop)
findings.finding: Closing the overlay via × or by clicking outside the sheet discards any unsaved matching-rule changes immediately, with no confirmation or discard prompt.
findings.user_impact: A user who has just set up or edited the matching rule and dismisses the overlay by the × (a very common 'I'm done' gesture) or an accidental outside click loses the entire configuration silently — the rule reverts to whatever was last saved with no indication anything was lost, so the user believes the task is complete when it is not.
findings.suggested_fix: Before discarding, compare the draft to the last saved rule and show a confirm/discard prompt (or an inline 'unsaved changes' warning) whenever the overlay is closed with a modified draft.

evidence.action: Reviewed closeOverlay() and its bindings: $('closeX').onclick = closeOverlay, and the backdrop click listener calls closeOverlay() when the click target is the backdrop itself; closeOverlay() only removes the 'open' class.
evidence.observed: No comparison between draft and saved state, no confirm dialog, and no 'unsaved changes' warning exists anywhere in the close path — the sheet just disappears and the in-progress draft is dropped, matching the state map's direct observation that closing with unsaved changes produced no discard prompt and the overlay closed immediately.

findings.element: GSP settings page — 'Cancel sync if there is no matching open invoice found for a payment' toggle (id gspCancel)
findings.finding: Toggling this switch produces no visible change anywhere on the settings page at the moment it's flipped; its only effect is a sentence inside the separate matching-rules overlay, which most users won't have open.
findings.user_impact: A user deciding this policy (part of setting up how payments apply to invoices) toggles it and sees nothing happen, so they can't tell whether it registered — they are likely to toggle it back and forth, or click the page's Update button unsure of what they are actually saving.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the toggle its own on-page state indicator (as the 'Configure matching rules' row already has with its 'Using defaults / Custom rules' badge), or move its plain-language consequence onto the settings page itself instead of only inside the overlay.

evidence.action: Read the gspCancel change handler: it only calls refresh() 'if ($("backdrop").classList.contains("open"))' — i.e. only when the matching-rules overlay happens to already be open — and traced plainEnglish(), the only consumer of gspCancel's value, which renders solely inside the overlay's 'plain terms' rail.
evidence.observed: With the overlay closed (its normal state when a user is on the GSP settings page), flipping gspCancel changes nothing visible on screen; no badge, hint, or text near the toggle updates, unlike the adjacent 'Configure matching rules' control which has a persistent status label.

findings.element: Matching-rules overlay — metadata 'Key' input (shown when source is Payment metadata / Invoice metadata)
findings.finding: The Key field's required status is invisible until the user presses Update: the placeholder just says 'Key' with no required marker, and the 'Required' error only renders after a failed submit attempt.
findings.user_impact: A user filling in a custom rule with a metadata source can complete the rest of the form believing it's ready, click Update, get rejected, and have to notice and fix a field whose necessity was never signaled up front — for anyone who abandons after that first rejection, the rule is never saved.
findings.suggested_fix: Mark the Key field as required at render time (e.g. an asterisk or inline hint) instead of only after a failed submit, so the requirement is visible while the user is still filling in the row.

evidence.action: Reproduced the state map's recon step (select 'Payment metadata' as the source, leave Key empty, click Update) and read the supporting code: submitAttempted is false until saveBtn.onclick sets it true, and applyFieldErrors() — the only place that adds the 'Required' text/invalid state — returns immediately whenever submitAttempted is false.
evidence.observed: Overlay stayed open and a 'Fix the highlighted fields' banner plus a 'Required' message appeared under the Key input only after Update was pressed with the field empty; before that click, the empty Key input carries no required indicator at all.
